landmarks.name: Alderlobe Roads
landmarks.note: A dark mouth in the cliff foot that the tide fills twice a day and empties again.

landmarks.name: Withyspit Geo
landmarks.note: A stream that runs off the cliff lip and never reaches a beach, because there is none.

landmarks.name: Brightrun Roads
landmarks.note: A finger of shingle the drift keeps building out across open water, growing every year.

landmarks.name: Bitternreef Roads
landmarks.note: Shallow brackish water penned behind a bar, calm when the sea outside is not.

landmarks.name: Head among Withystrand
landmarks.note: A neck of sand and shingle joining an island to the shore; it drowns on the big tides.

landmarks.name: Head at Lagoonbar
landmarks.note: A dark mouth in the cliff foot that the tide fills twice a day and empties again.

landmarks.name: Reedstrand Roads
landmarks.note: A bank of sand grown right across a bay mouth, shutting the water in behind it.

landmarks.name: Quilllobe Stack
landmarks.note: A rib of rock the waves have holed clean through, still standing on two legs.

landmarks.name: Head between Tidalfall
landmarks.note: A neck of sand and shingle joining an island to the shore; it drowns on the big tides.

landmarks.name: Head between Osierbar
landmarks.note: An old shoreline stranded above the present one, level enough to build a road on.

landmarks.name: Marramstrand Reach
landmarks.note: A spread of stone and grit laid out where a steep stream hits the flat and slows.

landmarks.name: Loambar Confluence
landmarks.note: Flat ground ribbed with the ghosts of old bends the river has already abandoned.

landmarks.name: Lagoonrun Confluence
landmarks.note: A gravel shallow where the river spreads wide enough to walk, in the right season.

landmarks.name: Loamholm Confluence
landmarks.note: The river gives up and splits, laying its load down in a fan of shifting channels.

landmarks.name: Marramrun Confluence
landmarks.note: A wide bed of gravel bars where the river runs in a dozen shallow threads at once.

landmarks.name: Sedgerun Fen
landmarks.note: A tangle of stilt roots standing in salt mud, impassable except by the tide channels.

landmarks.name: Mire within Loamlow
landmarks.note: A dome of peat that has grown above the water table and drinks nothing but rain.

landmarks.name: Willowfall Carr
landmarks.note: A patch kept permanently wet by water rising from below, greener than all round it.

landmarks.name: Mire of the Osiershallow
landmarks.note: Grass and channel by turns, walkable at low water and not at high.

landmarks.name: Marrameyot Carr
landmarks.note: Wet scrub of willow and alder, thorny, and slower to cross than open water.
